label: Food Insecure Population
contestNote: UPDATED Jul 14, 2026: UN Humanitarian Coordinator George Conway confirmed a 'real and credible risk of famine' in Burhakaba District (Bay Region) — the first district-level famine-risk confirmation of the crisis. WFP (Jun 28) reaching only 450,000 people (down from 2.2M in early 2025) as 2M enter IPC Phase 4 Emergency (double the prior year); 1.9M children face acute malnutrition; 76% of the IPC-4 population has no assistance pipeline through August. Nationally, 570,000+ need water assistance and 400,730 children face acute malnutrition (97,150 severe). HRP still only 15.2% funded as of Jul 14; over 500 health/nutrition facilities closed for lack of funds; water-trucking costs more than doubled in some areas.
delta: Burhakaba famine risk CONFIRMED (Jul 14) — first district-level famine-risk finding of the crisis; HRP still 15.2% funded
deltaNote: UN (Jul 14, 2026): 'The humanitarian context in Somalia is worsening faster than we originally projected... without immediate and sustained support from donors, the diaspora and the private sector, we risk a preventable catastrophe.' Somalia Humanitarian Fund allocated $4.7M to Burhakaba (incl. $2M reserve). No confirmed WFP full operational shutdown, but reach has fallen to roughly 1-in-5 of the early-2025 caseload.

label: AUSSOM Authorized Strength
delta: US tells AU it will end UNSOS funding support after AUSSOM's Dec 31, 2026 mandate expiry
deltaNote: In a July 1, 2026 letter to the African Union, the US said it will not support UNSOS — AUSSOM's logistics backbone (fuel, medevac, food, engineering, COE reimbursement) — beyond Dec 31, 2026, and will oppose any UNSC renewal including UNSOS support. Cites Somalia's failure to take ownership of security despite ~$2B in UNSOS support plus $1.6B bilateral aid over a decade. AU Commission convened an emergency meeting; a senior African diplomat called the decision 'irreversible.' Lands directly atop the unresolved constitutional crisis — a major threat to the security architecture propping up the FGS against Al-Shabaab. Security Council Report (Jun 2026) separately noted AUSSOM had expanded to 49 locations (vs. 23 in the original operational concept), reflecting drawdown pause/reversal.

label: AFRICOM Airstrikes in Somalia (2026 YTD)
contestNote: At least 74 confirmed strikes in Somalia by July 13, 2026 — on pace to exceed 2025's full-year record of ~124-126. A ~40-day pause (May 7-Jun 14) ended with a strike near Kurtunwaarey, followed by a cluster of strikes and Danab ground raids in Lower Shabelle/Lower Juba (Kurtunwaarey, Route 109 NW of Kismayo, near Welmaro, Qumbi, Sablaale) through mid-July. Airwars documents credible civilian harm in multiple strikes; AFRICOM no longer reports casualty assessments.
deltaNote: AFRICOM PR #36755 (Jul 13) targets Al-Shabaab near Qumbi and Sablaale — same night as a Danab raid killing 7 (incl. a senior commander) in Sablaale district and separate SNA/international strikes killing 26 in Middle Shabelle. 2026 pace remains the highest on record for Somalia.

label: Piracy Hostages (Simultaneous, 2026)
source: IMO Secretary-General / IMB Mid-Year Report / Maritime Executive Jul 2026
contestNote: As of July 16, 2026: Honour 25 (IMO 9109735, 17 crew), Sward (IMO 9174244, 15 crew) and Eureka (IMO 1022823, 12 crew) remain hijacked — 44 seafarers total, none released despite talks reported 'advanced stage' (Jul 16). Conditions deteriorating: Honour 25 crew caught between two rival pirate factions after an armed clash near the ship; 5 crew including the Master suffering health problems; food reduced to rice, water unsafe. IMB's mid-year report (Jul 9-10) found Somalia the sole outlier in an otherwise 34-year-low year for global piracy: 27 vessels boarded Jan-Jun, 5 hijacked, Somali pirates accounting for 94% of hostages taken worldwide. A separate attempted hijacking (MV Golden Arsenal, Jul 1) was repelled by the Indian Navy before it became a hostage-taking. No rescues or ransoms paid on the 3 held vessels.
delta: IMO chief publicly appeals for release (Jul 6); ransom talks 'advanced' but unresolved (Jul 16)
deltaNote: IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez (Jul 6, reiterated at IMO Council Jul 8) called for 'urgent, coordinated and decisive international intervention' for the 44 hostages' release. PTI (Jul 16) reported ransom negotiations for all 3 vessels reached an 'advanced stage' involving flag states, shipowners, insurers, and sanctions-list vetting — but no payment or release confirmed. The earlier-reported 'possible 4th vessel' off Garacad (Jun 5) was not corroborated by subsequent IMO/IMB reporting, which consistently counts 3 vessels and 44 hostages.
